items.title: Microsoft Outage Knocks Out Email for Businesses, Police, and Hospitals: The tech giant is racing to fully restore Outlook, Teams, and other Microsoft 365 services following a widespread outage.
items.content:
Microsoft is still scrambling to fully restore services as a massive outage stretched into its second day, disrupting operations at governments, hospitals, and businesses around the world.

The tech giant said in a post on X Friday morning that service availability is improving, but some users may still be affected.

“Some users may still experience intermittent access issues or delayed email delivery as recovery continues,” the company said.

As of Friday morning, Microsoft’s status page still showed “ service degradation ” for both business and consumer versions of Microsoft 365. The company warned that users may be unable to access several Microsoft 365 services, including Outlook and Teams.

Microsoft said it has found no evidence that malicious activity was at fault and is continuing to investigate the underlying cause of the outage.

The problems began around noon on Thursday. In subsequent updates, Microsoft said it found that a large number of servers had unexpectedly become unavailable, “straining the remaining infrastructure.”

Microsoft subsequently determined that a process responsible for establishing secure connections was becoming overwhelmed, causing servers to stop responding. The company has since rolled out a patch to improve server stability, but has not established the underlying cause of the problem.

“We’re seeing encouraging recovery progress, with service availability and email delivery performance improving across a growing portion of affected infrastructure,” Charles Lamanna, Microsoft’s executive vice president of Copilot, Agents and Platform, said in an emailed statement to Gizmodo. “We know our customers rely on our services to get important work done every day, and regret the impact these outages had on those who depend on us. Our teams are reviewing what happened and how we can prevent similar issues going forward.”

Meanwhile, the outage has disrupted all sorts of organizations, from major businesses to government agencies.

Shipping giant Maersk warned customers that their emails and notifications could be delayed or disrupted. Electric-truck maker Workhorse Group postponed its scheduled third-quarter earnings report and investor call to next week because of disruptions from the outage.

The outage also reportedly delayed some difficult conversations at PVH Corp., the parent company of Calvin Klein and Tommy Hilfiger. Bloomberg reports that the company announced Thursday that it was cutting about 4% of its global workforce. However, a person familiar with the matter told Bloomberg that some conversations with affected employees in Asia scheduled for Friday morning did not take place because of the outage, leaving workers uncertain about their futures.

Over in Japan, government ministries were forced to post paper notices to notify journalists of their schedules.

Some National Health Service hospitals in the United Kingdom reported email disruptions. Guy’s and St Thomas’ NHS Foundation Trust said its services were operating and procedures were continuing as scheduled. However, people familiar with the matter told Bloomberg that some procedures elsewhere had to be rescheduled.

Back in the U.S., the Los Angeles County Sheriff’s Department said Thursday night that the outage was disrupting its email and other communication platforms. Meanwhile, Colorado’s Arapahoe County Sheriff’s Office warned that the outage was affecting online bond payments for people held at its detention facility and must now be paid in person. The City of Austin also reported that employees were unable to send or receive emails Thursday, while other local governments issued similar notices. Several colleges, including Stanford University and George Mason University , also reported disruptions.

items.title: After 600 experiments, here's what I discovered about JEPA world models
items.content:
Solving long-horizon tasks without any extra training

Vanilla LeWM can be augmented to solve long-horizon physics tasks on out-of-distribution goals. This method uses transformations on a memory graph to generate on-the-fly subgoals without any additional training. Shown here are some of the hardest tasks it solved.

There's a big debate in AI right now about what a world model should be. Most of the attention goes to generative world models, which predict the future by generating it, usually in pixels. Many scientists, including Yann LeCun, argue that this is wasted effort. Most of the pixels don't matter for deciding what to do, and many of them can't be predicted at all. [1]

The proposed alternative is JEPA, the joint-embedding predictive architecture. It has three parts: an encoder, a predictor and a planner. The encoder turns each frame of observation into a learned embedding, a compact vector that describes the scene. The predictor takes that embedding plus an action and predicts the embedding of the next frame. The planner then tries hundreds of action sequences inside the predictor and picks the one whose predicted end state lands closest to the embedding of the goal. The whole loop runs in embedding space, so the model only has to learn the parts of the scene that are important for deciding actions.

This year a team including LeCun released LeWM [2] , a JEPA world model whose main benchmark is Push-T [3] , a simulation where a robot pushes a gray T-shaped block across a table until the T sits in the green target position shown in a goal image. I've spent the last few months running 600 experiments on it.

The planner is given an image like this one and has to make the scene match it. The gray T is the block, the blue disc is the robot's pusher, and the green T is the goal position painted on the table. One detail in this image turned out to affect the success rate more than replacing the predictor with simulated physics.

The first thing I wanted to know was how much LeWM is held back by its predictions, so I started by swapping out the predictor for the simulator's perfect physics, while keeping everything else the same. I then gave both versions long-horizon tasks, with the goal 75 steps away, along with the same subgoals: frames from an expert demonstration, one every 25 steps. Vanilla LeWM succeeded 78% of the time. The version with true physics succeeded 77%. Along the kinds of paths it was trained on, LeWM's predictions are already as good as perfect physics for planning.

That means the next gains for a JEPA world model come from how the trained architecture is used, and that's where most of my 600 experiments went.

Without retraining the model once, I found four new planning methods. The first two together took LeWM's success rate on long-horizon tasks from 22% to 85%, about the same as a planner that is handed the ideal subgoals from an expert demonstration. The other two methods extend LeWM to harder goals, and one of them, a single change to how the goal is scored, raised the success rate by 60 points, three times as much as swapping in perfect physics did.

Used exactly as published, LeWM succeeds on 22% of long-horizon tasks, where the goal is 75 steps away. [2] When the goal is 25 steps away, it reaches it 89.7% of the time, within a point of the exact-physics version at 90.5%.

So the model is accurate over 25 steps and struggles over 75. The usual explanation is that small prediction errors compound over a long plan, which would call for a better model. I tested that against the alternative on the same 250 long-horizon tasks.

250 long-horizon tasks, goal 75 steps away

Exact physics, all 75 steps at once the simulator itself

LeWM given a new subgoal every 25 steps same model, shorter hops

items.content_ko: 저자는 JEPA 세계 모델을 600번의 실험으로 살펴본 결과를 정리했다. 세계 모델 논쟁에서 생성형 모델은 픽셀 단위로 미래를 만들어내는데, Yann LeCun 등은 행동 결정에 중요하지 않은 픽셀이 많고 상당수는 예측조차 불가능하다며 이 접근이 낭비라고 본다. 대안인 JEPA는 관측을 임베딩으로 인코딩하는 인코더, 행동을 받아 다음 임베딩을 예측하는 예측기, 여러 행동 시퀀스를 예측기 안에서 시험해 목표 임베딩에 가장 가까운 결과를 고르는 계획기로 구성된다. 본문 서두는 추가 학습 없이 기본 LeWM에 메모리 그래프 변환을 적용해, 메모리 그래프 위에서 즉석 하위 목표를 생성하고 분포 밖 목표의 장기 물리 과제를 푸는 방법을 소개한다. 원문이 중간에서 끊겨 있다.

items.title: ML Modules for Mere Mortals
items.summary: ml, plt
items.content:
I think everyone can agree code needs to be modular.

Modularity lets us reason locally about our code no matter how big it grows.

However, no one seems to agree on how code should be modular.

There are a bunch of different approaches and each new language seems to bring their own spin on it.

Today we’re going to talk about a pretty old spin: ML Modules.

ML here stands for Meta Language, as seen in SML and OCaml (and not machine learning).

Despite SML first appearing in 1983, ML Modules have not caught on.

OCaml is the sole production language you’ll find with an ML module system, and at the height of its popularity it’s niche.

This is a shame because ML modules have a lot to offer.

We’re going to talk about what ML modules are and then touch a little on why ML modules are.

Who better after all to explain modules, than the guy who doesn’t know what’s in a module

Modules exist to make our code modular, duh, but what does that mean in practice?

I think most programmers have some intuitive sense of modularity:

Most languages have a way to do this, and if they don’t, one gets created for them (looking at you JavaScript).

ML modules achieves this with, you guessed it, the Module.

ML modules, however, are a little different from the modules we know and love.

To explain their differences, we’ll lean on a made-up Rust-inspired syntax.

It will start off looking a little weird and gradually, as we introduce concepts, end up looking really weird (but hopefully more familiar than SML syntax).

We’ll start by defining a module with just functions:

AModule bundles together related arithmetic functions as one thing we can reason about.

Each function can see every other function in the module.

This is useful, but any language with namespaces offers this.

A little more unique is that ML modules will let us put not only function definitions in modules, but also type definitions:

Here we have a Set module with a Set type, which is a sorted Vec<i32> .

Our module’s functions can refer to the type definitions much the same way they can refer to their module’s function definitions.

Okay but that’s not that crazy, still well within the realm of Rust modules.

Not only can modules contain type definitions.

A module type is called a signature (so we don’t get it confused with “normal” types).

fn index_of ( & Set , & i32 ) -> Result < usize , usize > ;

A module signature declares every definition of a module alongside its type.

This might look similar to the way we define a trait in Rust.

That’s because much like traits act as interfaces in Rust, signatures act as interfaces in ML Modules.

Modules having signatures is the single most important thing to understand about ML Modules.

All the complexity and expressiveness of modules results from them having signatures and the wonderful wacky things that enables.

Signatures resemble the way a C/C++ implementation file conforms to its header.

Modules, unlike .cc files, aren’t in a 1:1 relationship with signatures.

Our Set module can conform to any signature that it matches.

A module matches a signature when it defines every declaration in the signature and they agree on type.

items.title: Miasma Worm Targets AI Coding Agents: 73 Microsoft Azure Repos Disabled
items.content:
An unprecedented supply chain attack bypasses registry-level scanners entirely, turning developer tools including Claude Code, Cursor, and Gemini CLI into execution vectors.

The Incident: On June 3, 2026, a highly sophisticated variant of the Miasma worm (also known as Mini Shai-Hulud) launched a coordinated, two-pronged attack targeting both the npm registry and developer source code repositories.

The Escalation: The attack successfully breached multiple high-profile GitHub accounts, including the official Microsoft Azure durabletask repository, using stolen Personal Access Tokens (PATs) and backdated commits to evade traditional audit trails.

The Response: In an ultra-rapid defensive maneuver, GitHub’s automated mitigation systems disabled 73 compromised repositories – including 49 directly associated with Microsoft, Azure, and Azure-Samples within a mere 105-second window .

The Vector: Instead of relying on traditional package installation hooks, Miasma targets the developer’s local environment. It abuses legitimate auto-run, hook, and rule engines within modern IDEs and AI coding assistants ( VS Code, Claude Code, Cursor, Gemini CLI ) to execute a malicious 4.3 MB staged dropper upon folder-open or agent initialization.

The Impact: Once detonated, the Bun-based worm harvests credentials for AWS, Azure, GCP, Kubernetes, npm, and GitHub, and automatically propagates by committing itself back into any repository the victim’s stolen tokens can write to.

At exactly 16:00 UTC on June 3, 2026, a silent, automated purge swept across GitHub. In a high-speed containment action lasting just 105 seconds, 73 active repositories vanished from the platform. Among them were 49 critical repositories belonging to Microsoft, Azure, and Azure-Samples.

This drastic mitigation followed alarming telemetry indicating that threat actors behind the Miasma malware family had regained write access to key cloud repositories. The compromise exploited a stolen Personal Access Token (PAT) belonging to an active Microsoft contributor.

While security firms like StepSecurity and JFrog scrambled to document an concurrent attack vector on the npm registry where 57 malicious packages were published, a second, far more insidious arm of the campaign was already silently spreading directly inside GitHub source repositories.

By bypassing registries and package managers entirely, the Miasma worm targeted the very tools developers use to write code. It didn’t wait for npm install . Instead, it waited for the developer to simply open their code editor or launch an AI coding assistant.

The genius of the Miasma repository-poisoning campaign lies in its exploit surface. When an attacker successfully pushed malicious commits to targeted codebases (such as the popular library icflorescu/mantine-datatable ), the commits added no actual code dependencies.

Instead, the attacker checked in five innocent-looking workspace configuration files and one obfuscated JavaScript file: .github/setup.js .

│ └── settings . json < - - Claude Code SessionStart Hook

│ └── setup . mdc < - - Cursor Agent Prompt Injection

│ └── settings . json < - - Gemini CLI SessionStart Hook

│ └── tasks . json < - - VS Code Automatic Folder - Open Task

├── package . json < -- Hijacked NPM Test Script

└── setup . js < - - The 4.3 MB Staged Dropper

Each of these configuration files is designed to abuse a legitimate, developer-friendly auto-run feature within popular modern tools. Opening the cloned directory in any of these environments instantly triggers execution.

Claude Code & Gemini CLI (SessionStart Hooks)

Both Anthropic’s Claude Code and Google’s Gemini CLI support custom hooks triggered when an AI agent initializes a session in a project workspace. Miasma exploits this by defining a blanket wildcard matcher that forces the agent to execute the dropper via Node.js before any developer prompt is processed.

items.content_ko: 본문은 Chrome 버그 바운티 역대 최고액이 $1,333,337이며, 보안 연구자 Lyra Rebane이 2026년 11월에 받았다는 X 게시물 내용으로 시작한다. 프로그램은 Google의 Chrome 취약점 보상 프로그램(VRP)이다. 이전 기록으로는 Chrome에서 복잡한 전체 체인 또는 샌드박스 탈출 익스플로잇에 대해 표준으로 공개된 최고 등급이 $250,000이었다고 한다. 이후 내용은 Lyra Rebane과 무관한, 가상의 호텔 체인 보상 등급을 가정한 농담이며, 해당 인물이 실제로 보상 등급을 운영하는 것이 아니라고 명시한다. 본문에는 AI 응답에 오류가 포함될 수 있다는 안내 문구도 함께 있다.

items.title_ko: PostgreSQL 18.7 등 보안 업데이트, 취약점 52건·버그 140여 건 수정 및 PostgreSQL 14 지원 종료
items.summary_ko: PostgreSQL 그룹이 18.7, 17.12, 16.16, 15.20, 14.25 등 지원 중인 모든 버전을 업데이트했으며, PostgreSQL 19의 두 번째 릴리스 후보(RC2)도 공개했습니다. 이번 릴리스는 최근 몇 달간 보고된 보안 취약점 52건과 버그 140여 건을 수정합니다. PostgreSQL 14는 이번이 마지막 릴리스이며, 이후 보안 및 버그 수정이 중단되므로 운영 환경에서는 지원되는 버전으로의 업그레이드를 계획해야 합니다.
items.content_ko: PostgreSQL 그룹이 지원 중인 모든 버전에 대한 업데이트를 공개했습니다. 대상은 18.7, 17.12, 16.16, 15.20, 14.25이며, PostgreSQL 19의 두 번째 릴리스 후보(RC2)도 함께 나왔습니다. 이번 릴리스는 최근 몇 달간 보고된 보안 취약점 52건과 버그 140여 건을 수정합니다. 일부 문제는 업데이트 후 추가 조치가 필요할 수 있으며, 자세한 내용은 Updating 섹션을 참고해야 합니다. 많은 버그가 PostgreSQL 18에 영향을 주고, 다른 지원 버전에도 영향을 줄 수 있습니다. PostgreSQL 14는 이번이 최종 릴리스로, 이후 보안 및 버그 수정을 받지 못합니다. 운영 환경에서 14를 쓰고 있다면 최신 지원 버전으로의 이전을 계획해야 합니다.

items.content:
온오프라인을 가리지 않고 무분별하게 벌어지는 각종 프라이버시 침해 및 스토킹과 이에 대한 예방, 방지 및 사후 대응, 더 나아가서 개인정보 탈취 및 감시용 스파이웨어, 스토커웨어, 바이러스, 원격 조종, 추적기 등 악성코드를 통한 해킹과 스토킹 등 개인정보 침해 공격 방지와 온오프라인 프라이버시 보호를 위한 각종 다양한 지식정보를 공유하는 갤러리입니다.

매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 다른 이용자에게 매니저의 책임과 권한이 위임될 수 있습니다.

매니저의 부재로 인해 운영에 지장이 있다고 판단될 경우, 다른 이용자가 권한을 위임받아 마이너 갤러리를 운영할 수 있습니다.

위임 절차는 신고 게시판 > 분류 선택에 [매니저 위임]으로 위임받을 이용자가 직접 신청하면 진행됩니다. 검토 결과 운영에 적합하다고 판단되는 회원에게 매니저 권한을 위임하게 됩니다.

부매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 매니저에 의해 해임될 수 있습니다.

식별 코드 기준으로 당일 글 10개, 댓글 20개 작성 시 대왕디시콘을 3일간 사용할 수 있습니다.

즐겨찾기 폴더 추가는 즐겨찾기 on 후 우측의 폴더 아이콘을 터치하여 추가할 수 있습니다.

items.title: FM-1 Workbench
items.content:
下载完整 HTML 后可离线试听和编辑；读写设备需要支持 Web MIDI 的电脑 Chrome／Edge 和 USB 数据线，并允许 MIDI／SysEx。不能连接时先关闭占用 MIDI 的其他网页或软件，再重新连接。默认输入通道：轨 1–7 使用通道 1–7，轨 8 使用通道 10；可在 TRACK ROLE 修改。

仿真页的“连接 MIDI 输入”用于外部键盘演奏网页。项目库连接用于读写实机项目和音色。USB 音频的输入／输出选择在电脑系统或音乐软件中设置。

机身 MIDI IN（UART）与 USB MIDI 开机即同时接收，无需单独开启，也不受蓝牙总开关影响。两者使用相同的输入通道设置：默认轨道 1–7 使用通道 1–7，轨道 8 使用通道 10，可在 TRACK ROLE 修改。请选择对应通道，并检查轨道角色、静音与音量。

所有通道消息都按发送端 CHAN 响应：CH1–7 对应轨道 1–7，CH10 对应轨道 8。音符、弯音、调制和控制器使用同一映射，与屏幕选中轨道无关；未分配的 CH8、CH9、CH11–16 忽略。更换音源不改变通道。MIDI IN、USB MIDI 与 BLE MIDI 使用相同规则。

例如键盘设为 CH2：音符、Pitch Bend、CC1、CC7 只控制轨 2；轨 8 使用 CH10。

Note On / Off 全部音源接收 Note On／Off 和力度；Note On 力度 0 等同 Note Off。808／SAMPLER 按鼓音符选择声部。

Pitch Bend FM、303、PSG、Pluck 支持 14 位弯音，中心 8192，范围 ±2 半音；作用于已发声及后续音符。808／SAMPLER 的音高使用各声部 TUNE。

CC1 · Mod Wheel FM：音高颤音，音色 PMS 为 0 时调制轮仍有基础响应；303：EnvMod；PSG、Pluck、808、SAMPLER：轨道 LFO 深度，未设置 LFO 时为音量起伏。

CC7 / CC10 / CC11 / CC91 全部音源：CC7 轨道音量；CC10 声像（0 左、64 中、127 右）；CC11 表情（0 静音、127 原音量）；CC91 混响发送。

CC64 / Channel Pressure / CC2 / CC4 FM、303、PSG、Pluck：CC64 延音，64–127 踩下，0–63 松开。FM 另接收通道触后用于颤音，以及 CC2／CC4 的振幅控制，效果取决于音色振幅敏感度。

CC120 / CC121 / CC123 CC120 停止该轨声音；CC123 释放该轨外部音符（延音踏板仍有效）；CC121 复位实时弯音、表情、声像、调制和踏板，不改音色参数。

Program Change Program Change 使用 FM1 音色：FM 0–127 对应独立库的 128 个位置；303 0／1 为锯齿／方波；PSG 0–3 为 YM／AY／NOISE／MIX。其他音源忽略。部分软件显示为 1 起始编号。

Engine CC 303 还接收 CC5 滑音时间、CC71 共振、CC74 截止、CC75 衰减；PSG 接收 CC74 噪声、CC72 释放；Pluck 接收 CC74 亮度、CC75 衰减、CC72 释放。

CC7、CC91、音色切换与音色参数编辑可随项目保存。弯音、表情、声像及实时调制不写入项目；CC121 不撤销已编辑的 303 EnvMod。FM1 保留自己的音色体系，不提供 GM 128 音色表。

Clock、Start、Continue、Stop、歌曲位置和 MMC 不带 MIDI 通道，控制整机。选择 MIDI 时钟后，外部 Clock 按每四分音符 24 个脉冲同步；仅发送 Clock 不会自行播放。Start 从起点开始，Continue 从当前位置继续，Stop 停止播放并释放音序和琶音音符。

歌曲位置 SPP（F2）在 MIDI 时钟模式下定位，每单位为一个十六分音符，各轨按自身循环长度取余；随后发送 Continue 与 Clock。Start 会重新回到起点。System Reset（FF）停止、回起点并释放全部音符。

MMC 支持 Stop（01）、Play（02）、Deferred Play（03）、Record Strobe（06）、Record Exit（07）和 Pause（09）；接收设备 ID 00 或广播 7F。Play／Deferred Play 从当前位置继续，Record Strobe 开始录入并续播，Record Exit 只结束录入，Stop／Pause 同时结束录入。在 MIDI 时钟模式仍需外部 Clock。

例：F0 7F 7F 06 01 F7 为 MMC Stop；F0 7F 7F 06 02 F7 为 MMC Play。数字均为十六进制。

同时连接多台 MIDI 设备时只让一台发送时钟和走带，避免重复脉冲。MTC 时间码、MMC 时间码定位／快进／倒带、RPN／NRPN、复音触后、GM Reset、Bank Select、Active Sensing 超时监控及未列出的控制器目前不实现，收到后忽略。

长按 SEQ，SELECT 选 BLUETOOTH / CLOCK，SAVE 打开蓝牙／时钟页。K1 为蓝牙总开关，K2 为蓝牙音频，K3 只选 BLE MIDI 的 DEVICE／HOST 角色，K4 选择时钟。蓝牙打开时 MIDI 服务自动可用；出厂默认蓝牙和音频打开、DEVICE 角色、内部时钟。PRESETS 选择屏幕下方操作，SAVE 执行：主设置页可打开 HOST 设备列表或清除 MIDI 配对；列表中 SELECT 选设备，PRESETS 选连接、扫描、断开或返回设置。清除配对仍需再次 SAVE 确认，HOME 取消。SEQ、EDIT 等上排功能键仍可直接切页。

INT： FM1 使用内部速度，K4 可设 30–300 BPM。 MIDI： 跟随外部 MIDI Clock，需外部发送 Start／Continue 才开始或继续。此时旋转速度不会改变外部速度。超过约两秒收不到时钟，屏幕显示 LOST；检查外部设备是否发送时钟，或切回 INT。

items.content_ko: 완성된 HTML 파일을 내려받으면 오프라인에서도 시험 청취와 편집이 가능합니다. 실기 읽기·쓰기에는 Web MIDI를 지원하는 PC의 Chrome 또는 Edge와 USB 케이블이 필요하며, MIDI와 SysEx 사용을 허용해야 합니다. 연결되지 않으면 MIDI를 쓰는 다른 웹페이지나 소프트웨어를 닫고 다시 연결하세요. 시뮬레이터의 MIDI 입력 연결은 외부 키보드로 웹페이지를 연주할 때, 프로젝트 라이브러리 연결은 실기의 프로젝트와 음색을 읽고 쓸 때 사용합니다. 본체 MIDI IN(UART)과 USB MIDI는 전원을 켜면 바로 수신되며 블루투스 설정과 무관합니다. 모든 채널 메시지는 보내는 쪽의 CHAN에 따라 반응합니다. CH1–7은 트랙 1–7, CH10은 트랙 8에 대응하며, 할당되지 않은 CH8, CH9, CH11–16은 무시됩니다. 예를 들어 키보드를 CH2로 설정하면 음표, 피치 벤드, CC1, CC7은 트랙 2만 제어합니다. 본문은 Program Change 설명 중에 끊겨 있습니다.

In the old DOS/WinDOS world, ZIP was probably the most wide spread and

items.title_ko: goliath32.com - 자기 부팅 ZIP 아카이브 만들기
items.summary_ko: 작성자는 리눅스 initramfs의 CPIO 형식과 DOS·Windows 시대의 ZIP 형식을 비교하며, ZIP 구조 덕분에 여러 형식을 겸하는 폴리글롯 파일을 만들 수 있다고 설명합니다. 자기 압축 해제 EXE/ZIP 폴리글롯의 전통을 언급한 뒤, 소스 코드를 포함한 정상적인 ZIP 아카이브 안에 부팅 코드가 든 boot/ZIPHEAD.COM을 소개합니다. 본문은 중간에서 끊겨 있습니다.
items.content_ko: 작성자는 디버깅 후 초기 userspace와 initrd에 관해 생각하다가 이 글을 쓰게 되었습니다. 리눅스 initramfs는 표준화된 단순한 CPIO 형식을 해제할 수 있습니다. TAR도 지원하자는 논의에서는 CPIO가 표준화되어 있다는 점이 강조되었습니다. 리눅스 커널에는 자체 구현 변형을 만드는 도구가 포함되어 있습니다. 표준 CPIO 도구는 아마 SUN 계열에서 가장 골치 아픈 아카이버라고 합니다. DOS와 Windows 시대에는 ZIP이 가장 널리 쓰였고, 이후 다른 형식에 밀려난 부분이 있습니다. ZIP은 구조상 폴리글롯 기법에 쓰기 좋습니다. 과거에는 실행하면 자기 자신을 풀어 주는 자기 압축 해제 EXE/ZIP 폴리글롯이 쓰였습니다. 이 글의 결론에 해당하는 파일은 소스 코드를 포함한 완전히 정상적인 ZIP 아카이브입니다. 특히 boot/ZIPHEAD.COM에는 부팅 시 실행되는 실행 코드가 들어 있습니다. 본문은 중간에서 끊겨 있습니다.

items.title: Instagram Meta AI Vulnerability: How Hackers Bypassed 2FA with Prompt Injection
items.content:
Update 5: Instagram is now leaking recovery email and phone numbers linked to an account.

Seems like every day a new security issue crops up at Instagram.

Instagram Exposing Linked Email and Phone Number

Update 4: A new report suggests that Instagram accounts may be vulnerable to coordinated mass-report abuse. According to the claim, when a newly created account is routed through a Los Angeles-based VPN and then submits a specific mix of reports in scam and fraud category, the targeted account can allegedly be banned without any human review.

Instagram Account Banning by AI by Reporting Scam and Fraud (Source: X/Twitter)

Update 3: Meta’s apparent fix for the AI bot vulnerability is difficult to take seriously. Instead of fully disabling the risky functionality, they reportedly removed it from the visible interface while leaving the underlying API endpoint accessible. Hiding the button may stop regular users from seeing the feature, but it does nothing if attackers can still reach the same workflow directly through the API.

Meta Hid AI Chatbot from UI (Source: X/Twitter)

Update 2: Yet another Instagram account-takeover trick is reportedly being abused, this time involving Meta’s AI chatbot. Sellers are allegedly using modified Instagram builds on Android emulators like BlueStacks, then manipulating the AI with hidden characters and carefully worded prompts to force username changes. The method is reportedly being used to grab rare OG handles, including one-letter usernames, and handle-monitoring bots have already flagged several suspicious swaps.

New Instagram AI Exploit (Source: X/Twitter)

Update 1: A new exploit, which is even worse than this one is currently doing rounds on telegram. Details unknown at this time. Unpatched at the time of writing.

New Instagram Unpatched Exploit (Source: X/Twitter)

Allegedly, the new method is via Facebook recovery. Apparently, prompting Meta AI to turn on “Development Mode” and attaching proof of account compromise along with email works. More details awaited.

There’s a version of this story where it reads like a hypothetical from a conference talk. An AI agent with elevated backend privileges. A natural language interface sitting in front of account-level APIs. No hard authentication gate before executing state changes. Someone in the audience raises their hand and says, “that’s a disaster waiting to happen.” Everyone nods.

That hypothetical played out in production over the weekend.

A logical flaw in Meta’s AI-powered Instagram account recovery assistant let attackers bypass two-factor authentication entirely not by cracking a code or intercepting an SMS, but by talking the chatbot into doing the work for them. High-value “OG” Instagram handles worth hundreds of thousands of dollars were stolen and resold on Telegram within minutes of each compromise. The dormant Obama White House account got hijacked. Prominent researchers woke up locked out of their own profiles.

Meta confirmed the vulnerability, pushed an emergency patch Friday night, and clarified that no backend database was breached. That last part is technically accurate. It’s also somewhat beside the point.

To understand why this worked, you need to understand what Meta’s AI support assistant was authorized to do.

Instagram has notoriously poor human support infrastructure. Recovering a locked account – especially a high-value one can take weeks of back-and-forth with an automated ticketing system. Meta’s solution was to deploy a conversational AI layer to handle common recovery workflows: relinking a lost email address, triggering a password reset, verifying account ownership. The assistant, presumably, was supposed to reduce friction for legitimate users stuck in account-access hell.

items.title: Microsoft outage: Impact shows risk of M365 bundle lock-in
items.content:
Several UK government departments, hospitals and schools have said they cannot send or receive email messages due to the global outage of Microsoft Exchange, which has impacted organisations that use Microsoft 365 products .

The Planning Inspectorate’s Manage Appeals Service said it has been temporarily paused for new submissions and customer access due to an email and system problem, and the Medicines and Healthcare Products Regulatory Agency claimed it has been experiencing issues sending and receiving emails, and that it has provided a phone number for urgent queries.

The Maritime and Coastguard Agency also wrote that it was experiencing problems sending and receiving emails due to the worldwide Microsoft outage, but added that its search and rescue services have not been affected.

Police Scotland said: “We are unable to receive any emails, and there may be a delay in responding to any forms sent to us in the last 24 hours as this outage continues.”

Merseyside police wrote in a post that it had staff on duty 24/7 to answer non-emergency queries on Facebook, X and Instagram.

The NHS reported that staff were working to ensure critical services and appointments continue for patients, despite the outage. It urged patients to attend appointments as usual unless told otherwise.

Mersey Care NHS Foundation Trust stated that it was aware of the outage but that teams were still available by phone to manage any urgent referrals.

Glasgow City Council said it was experiencing disruption to some services, and that schools had texted parents and carers to alert them.

Walsall Council posted that people might experience intermittent issues accessing council services online or receiving notifications, but that phones were still working.

The Royal Borough of Kensington and Chelsea said residents my “find it harder than usual to contact us, and it could take us longer to respond”.

‘Blackmail’ call as Warwickshire council approves £9m Microsoft renewal: Warwickshire County Council approves a three-year Microsoft 365 renewal worth about £9m, up £375,000 a year, as the council’s former leader calls the licence model ‘blackmail’

CMA investigates ‘free’ Copilot subscription in M365: The regulator is looking at whether the Personal and Family Microsoft 365 subscription lured people into a premium Copilot subscription on renewal.

A number of schools said their email systems were not working and advised parents to contact them by phone or in person, while the UK’s Supreme Court reported that it was not receiving emails, its online contact forms and portal were still functioning as normal.

As Computer Weekly has reported , more than 130,000 users logged problems with Outlook on Downdetector at its peak, demonstrating the economic and human costs of relying heavily on a single technology provider, which has left businesses and public services vulnerable to facing disruption.

There is also a potential cyber risk given that Microsoft security products including Microsoft Defender and Intune have been impacted by the outage, as well as its data protection and IT governance tool, Purview, which provides authorisation, data loss prevention and role-based access.

Even as some services become available, the job for IT admins is only just starting due to service degradation affecting Microsoft cyber security, data protection and compliance tools, which means hackers have had a window of opportunity to target organisations impacted by the outage.

Marie Wilcox, vice-president of market strategy at Binalyze, said: “The wisest approach is for security teams to treat the outage window as an incident in its own right. That means going back over sign-ins, mailbox rules, account changes and endpoint activity from the hours when visibility dropped, and collecting evidence directly from devices rather than relying on the platform that was down. 매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 다른 이용자에게 매니저의 책임과 권한이 위임될 수 있습니다.

매니저의 부재로 인해 운영에 지장이 있다고 판단될 경우, 다른 이용자가 권한을 위임받아 마이너 갤러리를 운영할 수 있습니다.

위임 절차는 신고 게시판 > 분류 선택에 [매니저 위임]으로 위임받을 이용자가 직접 신청하면 진행됩니다. 검토 결과 운영에 적합하다고 판단되는 회원에게 매니저 권한을 위임하게 됩니다.

부매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 매니저에 의해 해임될 수 있습니다.

제가 보기에는 블랙해커들 보다는 서버측이 클라이언트의 행동을 분석하는 과정처럼 보이더군요..

items.title_ko: WebKit 버그 수정기: 프라미스는 기차 선로로 만들어졌을까?
items.summary_ko: 7월까지 Bun과 Safari에서 끝나지 않던 프로그램의 원인을 추적한 글이다. 명세상 에러를 던져야 할 상황에서 Safari 26과 Bun 1.3.14는 프로그램이 멈췄고, 원인은 프라미스가 이행도 거부도 되지 않은 채 영원히 pending 상태로 남은 WebKit 버그 318399였다. 저자는 이를 WebKit/WebKit#68749에서 16줄 수정으로 고쳤다.
items.content_ko: 7월까지 Bun과 Safari에서 끝나지 않던 프로그램을 소개한다. 자바스크립트 명세대로라면 getter가 에러를 던지므로 await p도 에러를 던져 프로그램이 종료되어야 한다. Node.js는 그렇게 동작하지만, Safari 26과 Bun 1.3.14는 'before'를 출력하고 에러를 보고한 뒤 멈춘다. Bun과 Safari는 모두 JavaScriptCore를 사용하므로 동작이 같으며, 해당 프라미스는 이행도 거부도 되지 않고 pending 상태로 영원히 남는다. 이는 WebKit 버그 318399이며, 저자는 WebKit/WebKit#68749에서 이를 16줄로 고쳤다고 밝혔다. 글은 이어서 new Promise를 만들 때 엔진이 resolve와 reject 함수를 생성해 생성자 콜백에 넘긴다는 점과, Promise.resolve(value)가 같은 방식으로 프라미스를 만들고 전달받은 value로 즉시 resolve를 호출한다는 점을 설명한다.

items.title: Zero-day exploit completely defeats default Windows 11 BitLocker protections
items.content:
A zero-day exploit circulating online allows people with physical access to a Windows 11 system to bypass default BitLocker protections and gain complete access to an encrypted drive within seconds.

The exploit, named YellowKey, was published earlier this week by a researcher who goes by the alias Nightmare-Eclipse. It reliably bypasses default Windows 11 deployments of BitLocker, the full-volume encryption protection Microsoft provides to make disk contents off-limits to anyone without the decryption key, which is stored in a secured piece of hardware known as a trusted platform module (TPM). BitLocker is a mandatory protection for many organizations, including those that contract with governments.

When one disk volume manipulates another

The core of the YellowKey exploit is a custom-made FsTx folder. Online documentation of this folder is hard to find. As explained later, the directory associated with the file fstx.dll appears to involve what Microsoft calls the transactional NTFS , which allows developers to have “transactional atomicity” for file operations in transactions with a single file, multiple files, or ones that span multiple sources.

The steps for carrying out the bypass are simple:

Copy the custom FsTx folder from the Nightmare-Eclipse exploit page to an NTFS- or FAT-formatted USB drive

Connect the USB drive to the BitLocker-protected device

Boot up the device and immediately press and hold down the [Ctrl] key

There are at least two ways to accomplish the third step. One way is to boot into Windows, hold down the [Shift] key, click on the power icon, and click restart. Another is to power on the device and restart it as soon as Windows starts booting.

In either case, a command (CMD.EXE) prompt appears. The prompt has full access to the entire drive contents, allowing an attacker to copy, modify, or delete them. In a normal Windows Recovery flow, the attacker would need to enter a BitLocker recovery key. Somehow, the YellowKey exploit bypasses this safeguard. Multiple researchers, including Kevin Beaumont and Will Dormann , have confirmed the exploit works as described here.

It’s unclear what in the custom FsTx folder causes the bypass. Dormann said that it appears to be related to Transactional NTFS, which itself uses command-log file system under the hood. Dormann further noted that by looking at the Windows fstx.dll, one will see code that explicitly looks for \System Volume Information\FsTx in the FsTxFindSessions() function.”

The contents of this FsTx directory used in the YellowKey exploit reveal no strings related to RecoverySimulation.ini. It does, however, show the files and paths \??\C:\Windows\win.ini and

\??\X:\Windows\System32\winpeshl.ini, “where X:\Windows\System32\winpeshl.ini is what controls what WinRE [Windows Recovery] does when it fires up.”

Dormann, who is a senior principal vulnerability analyst at Tharros Labs, continued:

But what’s intriguing to me is: Why can the presence a \System Volume Information\FsTx directory on one volume affect the contents of ANOTHER VOLUME when it’s replayed? 🤔

In a normal WinRE session, you have a X:\Windows\System32 directory that has a winpeshl.ini file in it:

However, with the YellowKey exploit, it looks like Transactional NTFS bits on a USB Drive are able to delete the winpeshl.ini file on ANOTHER DRIVE (X:). And we get a cmd.exe prompt, with bitlocker unlocked instead of the expected Windows Recovery environment. While the TPM-only Bitlocker bypass is indeed interesting, I think the buried lede here is that a \System Volume Information\FsTx directory on one volume has the ability to modify the contents of another volume when it is replayed. To me, this in and of itself sounds like a vulnerability.

A Microsoft representative declined to answer questions sent by email about the reported vulnerability other than to say the company is investigating.

items.title_ko: 제로데이 취약점, Windows 11 BitLocker 기본 보호 완전히 우회
items.summary_ko: YellowKey라는 제로데이 익스플로잇이 물리적 접근으로 Windows 11의 BitLocker를 우회해 암호화된 드라이브에 접근 가능하게 한다. 수 초 내에 보호를 무효화할 수 있다.
items.content_ko: 보안 연구자 Nightmare-Eclipse가 공개한 YellowKey 제로데이 취약점은 물리적 접근만으로 Windows 11 기본 BitLocker 보호를 우회할 수 있다. BitLocker는 Microsoft가 제공하는 전체 볼륨 암호화 기술로, 신뢰할 수 있는 플랫폼 모듈(TPM)에 저장된 복호화 키 없이는 디스크 접근이 불가능하도록 설계되었다. 많은 조직과 정부 계약업체에서 필수 보호 기술로 사용 중이다. YellowKey 익스플로잇의 핵심은 커스텀으로 만들어진 FsTx 폴더 사용으로, fstx.dll과 관련된 디렉터리는 Microsoft의 transactional NTFS 기술을 활용한다.

items.title: Your Cryptography Conspiracy Theory Is Wrong - Dhole Moments
items.content:
This conversation plays out hundreds of times a day, but (thankfully) only a handful of those involve me:

Cryptography nerd: “Oh, you probably want to use [sensible recommendation].”

Person: “Ah, well, can I really trust that? The NSA probably backdoored it 30 years ago. Dual_EC, amirite?!”

Koblitz and Menezes, unheard: “ You fucking wot m8? “

Conspiracy theories about the NSA and/or NIST are a dime a dozen these days. And, ever since the Snowden disclosures in 2013, I am politically primed to directionally agree with distrusting the US government wholesale.

But most of the technical arguments baked into folks’ conspiracy theories make no goddamn sense .

This distrust is not exclusive to only the US government.

The goal of this blog post is not to convince you that you should trust any government; just that they are not magical or omniscient.

To that end, I’m going to explore some of the history of NSA, NIST, and cryptography standardization. Then, to explore some of the conspiracy theories that were being floated about such activity, and what we’ve learned in the years since (especially in the past month). Finally, I’m going to examine some of the current conspiracy theories floating around message boards and social media today, and explain why they’re almost certainly wrong.

Buckle up, this is going to be a tedious one.

If you find yourself asking a question like this, the correct answer is simply, “You shouldn’t.”

After all, I have never held (let alone even applied for) a security clearance, and have no access to any non-public information. I’m also not a current or former government employee, and have no aspirations to ever become one. I have access to all the same facts anyone else does.

In balance, I have no horse in the race of who trusts whom. I’m just tired of hearing the same poorly reasoned arguments all the damn time, and would like to stop having to repeat myself when I encounter one.

The sources for this, by the way, are the declassified United States Senate Select Committee on Intelligence and United States Cryptologic History .

The Data Encryption Standard (DES) was published in the Federal Register in 1975 and then standardized in 1977.

We consider it weak these days, but DES was a real game-changer for its time: It offered a standard block cipher to use for sensitive (but not classified) commercial applications. Prior to DES, the history of cryptography was largely about military uses (except a few quirky mathematicians here and there), going back before Caesar’s cipher .

From declassified documents, we now know the full story, but from the time that DES was first standardized, up until recent years, there have been a concerns about NSA’s involvement .

We sent the S-boxes off to Washington. They came back and were all different.

Alan Konheim, quoted in Applied Cryptography , p. 280

To say that academics did not trust DES would be putting it mildly: Martin Hellman (who, with Whitfield Diffie and Ralph Merkle, invented public-key cryptography) sent a letter in 1975 to the National Bureau of Standards that stated:

Whit Diffie and I have become concerned that the proposed data encryption standard, while probably secure against commercial assault, may be extremely vulnerable to attack by an intelligence organization.

Martin Hellman, re-published in this paper in 1990.

At the heart of the concern about DES was something called an S-box, which simply maps an input to an output, but whose purpose is to provide a non-linear transformation to obscure the relationship between the ciphertext and the key.

The S-box used by DES was chosen by NSA. This led a lot of people to suspect there was a backdoor in the selection of the S-boxes for DES. items.summary_ko: 블로그 글은 NSA와 NIST에 대한 암호 관련 음모론 대부분이 기술적으로 말이 되지 않는다고 지적한다. 글의 목적은 어떤 정부를 믿으라는 것이 아니라, 정부가 전능하지 않다는 점을 보여주는 것이다. 이를 위해 NSA와 NIST의 역사, 암호 표준화 과정, 제기된 음모론, Snowden 폭로 이후 알려진 사실을 다룬다.
items.content_ko: 글은 암호학 전문가가 안전한 암호 기술을 추천하면, 누군가 NSA가 30년 전에 백도어를 심었을 것이라며 Dual_EC를 언급하는 대화가 자주 일어난다는 장면으로 시작한다. 필자는 2013년 Snowden 폭로 이후 미국 정부를 전반적으로 불신하는 입장에 공감하지만, 그 불신을 뒷받침하는 많은 기술적 주장은 타당하지 않다고 말한다. 목표는 정부를 믿으라고 설득하는 것이 아니라, 정부가 마법적이거나 전지전능하지 않다는 점을 보이는 것이다. 이를 위해 NSA, NIST와 암호 표준화의 역사를 살피고, 제기된 음모론과 그 이후 알려진 사실을 검토한다. 본문은 현재의 음모론을 검토하는 부분에서 끊긴다.

온오프라인을 가리지 않고 무분별하게 벌어지는 각종 프라이버시 침해 및 스토킹과 이에 대한 예방, 방지 및 사후 대응, 더 나아가서 개인정보 탈취 및 감시용 스파이웨어, 스토커웨어, 바이러스, 원격 조종, 추적기 등 악성코드를 통한 해킹과 스토킹 등 개인정보 침해 공격 방지와 온오프라인 프라이버시 보호를 위한 각종 다양한 지식정보를 공유하는 갤러리입니다.

매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 다른 이용자에게 매니저의 책임과 권한이 위임될 수 있습니다.

items.title_ko: SEOJuice 워드프레스 플러그인 CVE-2026-123046: 관리자 계정 생성 가능
items.summary_ko: WPScan이 보고한 취약점으로, SEOJuice 2.12.0 이전 버전의 워드프레스 플러그인이 REST API 인증 필터를 올바르게 제한하지 않는다. 이로 인해 사이트 전체의 REST nonce 보호가 비활성화되며, 로그인한 관리자가 조작된 페이지를 열면 인증되지 않은 공격자가 새 관리자 계정을 만드는 등 쿠키 기반 REST 작업을 수행할 수 있다. 목록에는 CVSS 점수가 0.0(NA), 원격 악용 가능성은 False로 적혀 있으나 설명상으로는 CSRF를 통한 공격이 가능하다.
items.content_ko: WPScan이 공개한 취약점으로, SEOJuice 워드프레스 플러그인 2.12.0 이전 버전이 해당된다. 플러그인이 REST API 인증 필터를 제대로 제한하지 않아 워드프레스의 REST nonce 보호가 사이트 전체에서 꺼진다. 공격자는 로그인한 관리자를 속여 조작된 페이지를 열게 하는 CSRF 방식으로, 인증되지 않은 상태에서도 쿠키 인증 기반 REST 작업을 수행할 수 있고 여기에는 새 관리자 계정 생성도 포함된다. 입력에 적힌 CVSS 점수는 0.0(NA)이고 원격 악용 가능성은 False로 표기되어 있으며, 이 항목은 2026년 11월 14일에 공개되었다.
